0002.text: Nature gives nothing for free. Every scrap of power your Cunning Woman wields is bought with a life: your own people at the forest altar, captives dragged home by the Oss, whole crowds in the wicker. Burn too many of your own and the rest will flee into the woods.

0024.text: Watch the tribes fight among themselves

0026.text: Your tribe is ochre. {number}% land, {number} rival(s). Pale marks are the Moot and the hollow hills.

0028.text: Your game is restored, {number} minute(s) in.

0032.text: Tap your people to select them. Tap the ground to move them, or an enemy to attack.

0033.text: Drag with one finger to pan. Pinch to zoom, and twist two fingers to turn the world.

0034.text: Turn on Box, then drag to select a group. Double-tap a unit to select all of that kind nearby.

0035.text: To clear your selection, tap with two fingers at once, press and hold on empty ground, or tap the selection line above the tabs.

0037.text: Left-click selects your people, or tells the selected ones what to do; drag to box-select. Right-click on empty ground clears the selection; right-click on something still commands.

0038.text: Right-drag turns the view, middle-drag or WASD pans, the wheel zooms. Space finds your Cunning Woman, keys 1–0 pick spells, F toggles full screen, Esc cancels.

0040.text: Villagers chop wood, build, and go into huts to breed. Breeding is the heart of everything, because the only mana is what you give back to nature.

0041.text: The forest altar takes one offering at a time and is stronger the more trees stand around it. The wicker man takes five and burns, giving mana and a frenzy of speed. The Wicker God takes twelve and burns for an enormous offering, terrifying any enemy who sees it. Both wicker figures burn down and must be rebuilt.

0042.text: Burning your own people fills the dread meter. Past the mark, frightened villagers start slipping away into the wilds. Dread fades with time, and faster with more huts.

0043.text: Osses, from the Oss House, roam the ground around where you last sent them and seize anyone they can catch, wildmen or enemy, carrying them home to your thrall fold at a run. Once an Oss has a captive it will not take orders until it is home. Captives are worth far more than your own people and cause no dread; kill an Oss on its way home and its captive goes free. You start with one thrall fold, which holds fifteen. Two or more captives left together in a fold will breed, slowly at first and then faster, so a fold left alone fills itself.

0044.text: Herne's Oak is a vast dead tree raised in deep woodland. Hang your Cunning Woman from it for two minutes, during which she can do nothing, and the Wild Hunt rides for you: antlered horsemen who roam the whole world killing anyone they find outside the reach of an enemy Cunning Woman. Every death they cause feeds you as richly as a captive, and lost riders return.

0045.text: Build a Maypole and idle villagers will dance around it, easing your people's dread. After enough merriment a May Queen is crowned. The longer she lives, the more her offering is worth, up to a vast sum with no dread and a long frenzy. Select fighters and tap her to swear them as her guards; you can do the same for your Cunning Woman. Rival Osses will hunt her, and a captured Queen can be offered by her captors for her full worth.

0046.text: Blackthorn hedges are cheap thorny barriers. Choose the hedge, tap where it starts and where it ends, and villagers plant it a length at a time. Nothing walks through a finished hedge, your own people included, so leave gaps; enemies must go round or hack through, which turns open ground into chokepoints.

0047.text: Your Bog is a hidden trap: your own people cross it safely, but enemies cannot see it and march straight in. It lasts until it has drowned ten of them. Fighters near their own buildings also take slightly less damage.

0048.text: When a rival army sets out for you, a horn sounds and the marching column shows on your map through the fog. An attack that loses half its strength breaks and runs home.

0049.text: The Rook Tree is a lookout in a dead tree. It sees a long way and hurls fire-pots at any enemy balloon in range, bringing one down in three hits. It ignores everything on the ground.

0050.text: Send fighters to your oak, your tomb or a hollow hill and they are posted there as guards. Guards stay put and are left out when you select your army.

0051.text: A tribe that loses every building, trained unit and its Cunning Woman is finished: its last villagers are dragged off as captives by whoever broke it. A tribe whose people are all dead hands its empty buildings to the conqueror, with an offering of mana.

0052.text: Ground where a building has been razed is salted: for three minutes its old owner cannot build there. A rival that falls to a fifth of its greatest size is broken. Its people gather at their stone circle where everyone can see them, its halls fall in and its Cunning Woman does not return; destroy its last fighters and the rest are yours.

0053.text: Tap a rival's marker at the top of the screen to look at where its people are. Tap again to move on to the next group.

0054.text: Training buildings turn a villager into a warrior, archer, Oss or balloonist.

0055.text: To cross water, have your Cunning Woman raise a Land Bridge from the shore towards the land you want. Anyone can walk it, your enemies included.

0056.text: Balloonists drift above the fighting and drop charges. Only other balloonists can reach them.

0057.text: Wildmen wander the wilds. They make easy captives.

0058.text: Hollow hills lie out in the wilderness. Bring your Cunning Woman to one with twenty followers and at least 1,500 mana and she is sealed inside for good. The hill becomes a wicker fortress: from it she sees everything and casts anywhere at half the mana. If enemies tear it down she is lost for a minute, then rises at your stone circle, and half your mana goes with her.

0059.text: All-against-all needs an unlit wicker man, ten followers to burn and a full bar of mana. Every hut falls, and every soul walks to the Moot at the world's heart to fight to the end.

0060.text: Pick a spell and tap a target. Your Cunning Woman walks into range and casts. If she dies she returns at your stone circle after forty-five seconds, as long as your tribe survives.

0061.text: The Scrying Torch plants a burning beacon where the Cunning Woman aims it. The land around it stays in sight for as long as it stands, which makes it a lookout over a pass, a rival's door or a hollow hill. Enemies can tear it down.

0062.text: You win when every rival tribe has no followers or buildings left.

0214.text: Across the water a people keeps its own fires and will not answer when we call. Our Cunning Woman has no power of her own: everything she does must be paid for with a life. Build a forest altar among the trees and give it villagers, one at a time. With what it gives back, raise warriors, lift the sea floor into a road, and cross.

0216.text: The grove gives a little for each life. The wicker man gives far more, but it takes five at once, and it must burn to give anything at all. Feed it, and the Cunning Woman will have what she needs.

0218.text: The wild folk wander the woods with no hearth and no name. The Oss will bring them in. Fill the fold with ten of them and the people will know we can feed the fires for a long winter.

0220.text: This neighbour is not idle. Their warriors will come. Archers behind a line of spears will meet them, and the Cunning Woman can turn a blow aside.

0222.text: Two peoples have smelt our smoke, and both are coming for us. We cannot beat them and we have no camp to raise more warriors. But our valley is ringed with crags, and there are only three ways in. Plant blackthorn across the gaps, wake the bog beyond them, sink the ground under anyone who forces a way through, and hold the village for ten minutes until they tire of us. The altar gives twice what it usually does here; feed it.

0224.text: Up here the land is broken into crags and there is barely room for two huts. Nobody can grow until they make level ground. Feed the altar, flatten the rock around the village, and build on what you make. Across the rocks one other people is just as cramped, and the first to spread out will win.

0226.text: Every people here keeps its own island, and the sea is too deep and too wide for any bridge. Our enemies have learned to fly. Their balloonists drop fire on the huts and carry fighters over the water. Here a Cunning Woman does not come back: if ours dies we are finished, and if theirs dies so are they. Keep fighters sworn to her side, keep the Rook Trees watching, and when you are ready, put her in a balloon.

0228.text: Raise the pole and let the people dance. When the merriment is high enough a Queen will be crowned. Keep her safe while she ripens, and then give her to the fire. Three Queens must burn before the summer is ours.

0230.text: Twelve go into the belly of the ram and the whole world sees it burn. Fill it with strangers and the Cunning Woman will shake the earth beneath our enemies.

0233.text: Out in the wilds the old hills are hollow. Walk the Cunning Woman there with twenty of the faithful and fifteen hundred mana and she will never walk again; but she will see everything, and reach everywhere.

0235.text: In the deep wood stands the dead oak. Hang the Cunning Woman from it for two minutes and the Hunt will ride for us, and every life they take will be ours. No wicker will burn in this wood, and our rivals know what the oak means: the moment she hangs, they will come for her. Guard the tree.

0238.text: Three peoples share these hills with us, and none of them will share for long. The mountains themselves can be made to burn.

0240.text: Four peoples on four islands, and no road, wing or spell will carry anyone across. There is only one way this ends. Grow, fill the wicker man, gather a full bar of mana, and call every soul to the stones at the heart of the world to settle it there.

0242.text: The year turns cold and the rivals are hungry. Everything you have learned is yours to use.

0244.text: From here the land is not kind. Three peoples, each as cunning as we are. Nothing is held back from us, and nothing from them.

0246.text: We have settled in the middle of everything. Every road leads to our door, and every army will take one.

0248.text: We arrive with little, and the others have been here for years. Their halls are built and their warriors drilled. We must be cleverer than them, because we cannot be stronger.

0250.text: Something has stirred the neighbours to fury. They will come early and often. Make them pay for every step.

0252.text: The sea has taken most of the world. What land is left is small and fought over, and the others are richer in offerings than we are.

0254.text: This is the end of the year, and perhaps the end of us. Three strong peoples surround us and they have already begun. Only the bog, the thorn, the hollow hill and the Hunt can turn this. Rejoice, if we live.
